lessonRef.title: Concept model C: deriving the hyperbola from the difference of focal distances

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±13, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.
Compare an oblique cylinder and a right cylinder with the same base area and the same height. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 7 and centre O. A point P lies 25 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle centred at P with radius 7; the tangent length is 24.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 24.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 18.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 24.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 5 and centre O. A point P lies 13 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 12.
